video_title: COMPLETE GAME CHANGER! Jaylen Brown & LeBron James JOIN FORCES

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James and Jaylen Brown joining forces in Philadelphia
quotes.excerpt: It's a complete game changer. It sets Philadelphia up to be the most fascinating storyline in the NBA.
quotes.quote: There is no doubt it's a complete game changer. It sets Philadelphia up to be the most fascinating storyline in the NBA because of Jaylen Brown, because of LeBron James, and what those two guys entail. Two former Finals MVPs joining an organization in an offseason—that's never happened in NBA history. So, that alone sets a precedent in the league. You have a team that already has Tyrese Maxey, you have Joel Embiid. There are going to be questions about this team, no doubt, but when you get Jaylen Brown, it puts you on the map, it puts you on the radar. It did for LeBron James and his decision-making process. But now that LeBron James actually goes and commits there, over Cleveland, over Miami, over Golden State, it puts them in a legitimate conversation, and everyone in Philadelphia now feels like they have a chance to win a championship.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's role in recruiting LeBron James to Philadelphia
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen Brown was 100% supportive of this move of getting LeBron James. To my knowledge, those two guys didn't speak during the process, but Jaylen Brown did have communication with Rich Paul during the process to let Rich Paul know that, 'Hey, I want LeBron here.'
quotes.quote: Jaylen Brown was 100% supportive of this move of getting LeBron James. To my knowledge, those two guys didn't speak during the process, but Jaylen Brown did have communication with Rich Paul during the process to let Rich Paul know that, 'Hey, I want LeBron here. This is someone I want to play with.' And so, those guys will eventually have their own conversation, LeBron and Jaylen will, and get on the same page. There will be plenty of opportunity for them to do so. But I think the big thing that I hear around the Sixers organization right now is sacrifice. When you think about scoring, you look at Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, on any given night, 1A, 1B. Joel Embiid is right up there as well, 1A, 1B, 1C. Either of those guys can lead this team in scoring on any given night. VJ Edgecombe can be a breakout on any given night. And then you look at LeBron James, and in a lot of ways, he's setting the table for everyone.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith's legacy compared to NBA greats
quotes.excerpt: If I get five, I pass Steph and I tie Magic, Kobe, Duncan with five chips. If I win back-to-back titles to end my career, I will have won with four different teams.
quotes.quote: If I get five, I pass Steph and I tie Magic, Kobe, Duncan with five chips. If I win back-to-back titles to end my career, I will have won with four different teams. Nobody has ever done that, and I would have tied MJ for six rings all-time in my career. I believe that was a factor. Is it something that their camp is willing to admit, or are we still in that world where they want to deny the obvious?

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' pursuit of a unique championship legacy
quotes.excerpt: LeBron is playing for a different legacy, and the legacy being being the only player in NBA history to win a championship with four different teams.
quotes.quote: It's always about the chips. It's always about the rings, and there's no doubt LeBron is playing for a different legacy, and the legacy being being the only player in NBA history to win a championship with four different teams. And this is kind of he's playing on borrowed time, right? A player has never gone into a 23rd season, much less a 24th and 25th season. So, it's like he's playing with some spare change here, where he can see, 'What can I do?' Even if I'm a starter, a high-level contributor, a high-level player to this, there's a very good chance if the Sixers win a championship, if they win a championship, Tyrese Maxey or Jaylen Brown or Joel Embiid have just as good, if not a better shot at winning Finals MVP, right? That's just because they're younger, they're more spry, their prowess for scoring is up there, they're in their prime ready to go.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's future and contract extension outlook
quotes.excerpt: I fully expect there to be contract extension talks come when he's eligible, I believe it's in late August.
quotes.quote: I fully expect there to be contract extension talks come when he's eligible, I believe it's in late August. They're going to discuss an extension, whether it's a one-year or a two-year extension that he's eligible for. They're going to give him one if he wants one. He, to my knowledge, I think there's going to be a desire on his part too. So there's mutual interest there. I think Stephen Curry understands where this organization is, that they're at a crossroads. They've gone after a bunch of stars over the years.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden State Warriors' missed opportunities in free agency
quotes.excerpt: They've swung and missed multiple times ever since that championship in 2022. They've not been able to get back to that mountain top.
quotes.quote: They've swung and missed multiple times ever since that championship in 2022. They've not been able to get back to that mountain top. They did get Jimmy Butler, though, and I think that was that one card that they had that they could say, 'Hey, as long as we have Jimmy, Steph, and Draymond, we have a shot to compete in the Western Conference.' The tough part is Jimmy Butler is going to miss a majority of next season. Moses Moody is going to miss a majority of next season. That's, I think, around $70 million in player's sideline for a majority of the season. I don't care what team you are. If you have that much money on the shelves not playing, you are in trouble. And so, this is just a team that right now is at a crossroads, they're somewhat stagnant. I don't know what move they can make without gutting their future.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.excerpt: In 24 days, they get Jaylen Brown and LeBron James and go from getting swept in the second round of the playoffs by the New York Knicks to being a favorite to capture the title.
quotes.quote: In 24 days, they get Jaylen Brown and LeBron James and go from getting swept in the second round of the playoffs by the New York Knicks to being a favorite to capture the title because of the acquisitions they've made in 24 days. I'm looking at that and I'm like, you know, I mean, what am I to think about Mike Dunleavy Jr. and Golden State, considering the job Bob Myers did there and clearly the job he's already doing with the 76ers?

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Davis's contract situation and trade rumors
quotes.excerpt: He's not really in control of the situation from the point of if the Wizards wanted to trade him, they could trade him.
quotes.quote: Like it was the trade deadline, he's not really in control of the situation from the point of if the Wizards wanted to trade him, they could trade him. But they also on August 6th can start discussing a contract extension. So, the Wizards though, they want to win. They didn't pay Trey Young $212 million on a max deal, they didn't draft AJ Dybantsa, they didn't go out and and and sign or acquire the types of players over the last calendar year just to say they got him. Like they want to compete in the Eastern Conference, and the only way you can compete when you have AD on your roster is hope that he's healthy and hope that he performs, and they're able to keep him healthy.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Kyrie Irving's injury status and recovery
quotes.excerpt: My understanding is Kyrie Irving's rehab has gone amazing. There was a sense during last season that, you know, if the Mavericks were playing at a very competitive level, like Kyrie Irving could have potentially come back in December, January.
quotes.quote: My understanding is Kyrie Irving's rehab has gone amazing. There was a sense during last season that, you know, if the Mavericks were playing at a very competitive level, like Kyrie Irving could have potentially come back in December, January, but given the way the season was going, and it obviously didn't make sense for for for the Mavericks either to rush Kyrie Irving back onto the floor. But from my understanding, he's fully recovered, 100% with that ACL tear from a couple seasons ago. He's been fully entrenched in the Mavericks' plans this offseason. Him and Dusty May, they've spoken, him and Masai Ujiri, the new president, they've spoken, Mike Schmitz, their new general manager, has spoken with Kyrie Irving as well. So they're entering next season, Patrick Dumont, the owner, he really wants to see Kyrie Irving, Cooper Flagg in this team next season and how that duo looks because, you know, Kyrie Irving is the other statesman of this team.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Minnesota Timberwolves' roster moves after missing out on LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: They have to bank on, you know, last season's success obviously and then you go you go out and get LaMelo Ball, that was the big star acquisition for them.
quotes.quote: They have to bank on, you know, last season's success obviously and then you go you go out and get LaMelo Ball, that was the big star acquisition for them. They did try to make overtures for LeBron James, but I never got the sense, I say, that they were a serious finalist here for LeBron. They were in the outer skirts, but they have a big hole at the four position. They still have not found a starter at the power forward spot. They trade away Jalen Duren, they trade away Naz Reid, and so that hole at the four position, that is of serious, I think when teams look at the Timberwolves, they look at that four spot as a serious concern right now.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Fred VanVleet's return and role for the Houston Rockets
quotes.excerpt: Fred VanVleet is fully expected to be back and playing. He missed last season with an ACL tear.
quotes.quote: Fred VanVleet is fully expected to be back and playing. He missed last season with an ACL tear that he had suffered in pre-training camp workouts last offseason. But he's fully healthy, he's aiming to be the starting point guard there and that gives this team a different look. I say the Rockets actually hired Chip Engelland from the Oklahoma City Thunder last week, and he's going to be an assistant for Ime Udoka. And if you remember his history, he's spent 17 years in San Antonio, he was basically the shooting guru there for Kawhi Leonard and a couple other players that came through there. Obviously spent a lot of time with Lou Dort and other players in Oklahoma City. He spent the last year, four years in Oklahoma City, he's won multiple rings in San Antonio and Oklahoma City. So he's joining the Rockets, that's going to be very interesting to see. You include him in a group that has Amen Thompson, Alperen Sengun, Reed Sheppard, he could have a pivotal role in as far as being a shot doctor there in Houston.
